CITY OF PASADENA
  City Council Minutes
  November 9 2020 - 2:00 P.M.
  City Hall Council Chamber

  SPECIAL MEETING
  The virtual meeting was convened pursuant to Executive Order N-29-20 issued by
  Governor Gavin Newsom on March 17, 2020, and was held solely by
  videoconference/teleconference

OPENING:  Mayor Tornek called the special meeting to order at 2:04 p.m. The
  pledge of allegiance was led by Councilmember Masuda.

ROLL CALL:  Mayor Terry Tornek
  Councilmembers:  Vice Mayor Tyron hlampton
  Councilmember Victor Gordo
  CouncilmemberJohn J. Kennedy
  Councilmember Steve Madison
  Councilmember Gene Masuda
  Councilmember Margaret McAustin
  Councilmember Andy Wilson

  Staff:  City Manager Steve Mermell
  City Attorney/City Prosecutor Michele Beal Bagneris
  City Clerk Mark Jomsky

CEREMONIAL MATTERS  Mayor Tornek announced that in honor of Veterans Day, the City's
  Veterans Committee in collaboration with Pasadena Media will
  present a special one hour tribute to be broadcast on KPAS at 11:00
  a.m., November 11, 2020; and presented a proclamation declaring
  November 11, 2020 as "Veterans Day," in the City of Pasadena.

SPECIAL ITEMS  COVID-19 UPDATE FROM DR. YING-YING GOH, PUBLIC
  HEALTH OFFICER
Councilmembers Gordo and
Kennedy joined the meeting  Dr. Ying Ying Goh, MD, Director of Public Health, reported on the
at 2:10 p.m. and 2:12 p.m.,  COVID-19 pandemic, providing information on the number of cases
respectively.  and deaths, hospitalizations and ICU admissions occurring in
  Pasadena, as well as at the state and national scale. She spoke on
  the need for the community to continue to practice safety measures;
  and business owners, and local institutions to increase vigilance
  when conducting symptom and exposure screening of employees
  and customers. Dr. Goh provided an update regarding schools and
  permits for in-person student instruction; the Health Department's
  flu vaccine drive-thru administration events; and reported on an
  award presented to Dr. Matt Feaster for his outstanding
  contributions during the pandemic for the benefit of the people of
  California and Pasadena; and responded to questions.

  The City Council thanked Dr. Goh and the Health Department staff
  for their hard work.

Council Minutes  1  11/09/2020
   Mark Jomsky, City Clerk, read aloud comments advocating for the
  reopening of in-class instruction for students from the following
  individuals:

  Erika Foy, Pasadena resident
  Mary Forrest, Pasadena resident
  Alyson Pernecky, Pasadena resident

  Following discussion, by consensus of the City Council, and on

  INCREASING CAPACITY OF LOCAL FOOD BANKS TO
  ADDRESS FOOD INSECURITY RESULTING FROM THE
  EFFECTS OF THE COVID-19 PANDEMIC
  Recommendation: It is recommended that the City Council:
  (1) Find that the proposed action is exempt from the California
  Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) in accordance with State CEQA
  Guidelines Section 15061(b)(3), the "general rule" that CEQA only
  applies to projects that may have an effect on the environment;
  (2) Appropriate $206,200 to Account No. 10518001-811400-
  56901, Parks, Recreation and Community Services Contract
  Services, and authorize staff to make necessary adjustments to the
  budget should 100 percent reimbursement not occur with utilization
  of unassigned fund balance if available or the General Fund
  Operating Reserve if necessary. This appropriation will cover food
  pantries and meal programs expenses from November 1, 2020 -
  January 31,2021;
  (3) Authorize the City Manager to expend an amount not-to-
  exceed $206,200, without Competitive Bidding pursuant to City
  Charter Section 1002(F), contracts for professional or unique
  services, with various Pasadena food pantries and meal programs
  as described in the agenda report;
  (4) Grant the proposed expenditures an exemption from the
  Competitive Selection process pursuant to Pasadena Municipal
  Code (P.M.C.) Section 4.08.049(B), contracts for which the City's
  best interests are served; and
  (5) Prioritize federal funding to increase the capacity of food bank
  programs in Pasadena to alleviate food insecurity experienced by
  City residents as a result of the COVID-19 pandemic. (Budget
  Amendment No. 2021-15)

  Steve Mermell, City Manager, provided introductory comments and
Mayor Tornek reported that  Jim Wong, Senior Project Manager, presented a Powerpoint
he is experiencing technical  presentation on the item, and responded to questions. Brenda
difficulties.  Harvey-Williams, Director of Parks, Recreation, and Community
  Services, provided information on the current food banks the City is
  supporting for food distribution to the community; and responded to
  questions.

Council Minutes  2  11/09/2020
   Councilmember Kennedy stated that his office is in contact with the
  Los Angeles Regional Food Bank, which has been providing
  groceries to those in need, but noted that the Food Bank is reporting
  insufficient staffing that is impacting continued food distribution
  efforts, and requested that staff consider providing minimal
  resources to ensure this important work continues.

  Councilmember Wilson and Vice Mayor Hampton expressed
  concerns with utilizing Community Development Block Grant
  (CDBG) funds to fund food programs without a detailed report on
  alternative programs that the CDBG COVID-19 designated funds
  might support.

  Councilmembers Gordo spoke in favor of working with the City's
  partnerships of local food banks to work with the Los Angeles
  Regional Food Bank and Los Angeles County to augment food
  distribution in the City; and asked staff to determine if any of the
  proposed funds might be used in other areas.

  City Clerk Jomsky, read aloud comments in support of the staff
  recommendation from the following individuals:

  Rosalind Thomas, Pasadena resident
  Paul Little, Pasadena Chamber of Commerce

D  Carl Paneno, representing St. Andrew's Catholic Church Food
  Pantry

  Following public comment, it was moved by Councilmember
  Wilson, seconded by Councilmember McAustin, to approve the staff
  recommendation:

  AYES: Councilmembers Gordo, Kennedy, Madison, Masuda,
  McAustin, Wilson, Vice Mayor hlampton
  NOES: None
  ABSENT: Mayor Tornek
  ABSTAIN: None

  PARTICIPATION IN GREAT PLATES DELIVERED PROGRAM
  Recommendation: It is recommended that City Council:
  (1) Find that this action is exempt under the California
  Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) in accordance with Section
  15061(b)(3) (Common Sense Exemption);
  (2) Appropriate $430,865 to Account No. 10518001-811400-
  56901, Parks, Recreation and Community Services Contract
  Services, and authorize staff to make necessary adjustments to the
  budget should 100 percent reimbursement not occur with utilization
  of unassigned fund balance if available or the General Fund
  Operating Reserve if necessary. This appropriation will cover the
  Great Plates Delivered expenses from October 10, 2020 -
  November 8, 2020;

  Council Minutes  3  11/09/2020
   (3) Determine if Pasadena should continue participation in the
  State's Great Plates Delivered program and, if so, consider a
  maximum of three additional months until February 7, 2021; and
  (4) Grant the proposed expenditure an exemption from the
  Competitive Selection process pursuant to Pasadena Municipal
  Code (P.M.C.) Section 4.08.049(8), contracts for which the City's
  best interests are served. (Budget Amendment No. 2021-16)

  Brenda Harvey-Williams, Director of Parks, Recreation, and
  Community Sen/ices, presented a Powerpoint presentation on the
  item, and responded to questions. Matt Hawkesworth, Director of
  Finance, provided information on staff's engagement with FEMA
  representatives; and responded to questions.

  Councilmember Masuda suggested that the City continue the Great
  Plates program for two additional months; spoke in favor of
  supporting local restaurants; and expressed concerns with the
  costs associated with continuing the program.

  Councilmember Wilson expressed concerns on the budgetary
  implications of continuing the Great Plates program, however,
  noted that the program is helping local restaurants and keeping
  individuals employed. He stated that he would be more inclined to
  pull back from the program if the partial re-opening of local
-^
  restaurants was imminent.

  Councilmember Gordo stated that it is not sustainable to expend
  funds to continue the Great Plates program given the City's
  finances. He spoke on the need for staff to transition the seniors
  who are participating in the Great Plates program to other food
  support options that the City supports, and inform the participating
  restaurants that the City can't afford to continue to subsidize
  approximately $466,000 a month. He reiterated his request for staff
  to provide a strongly worded letter to Los Angeles County
  Supervisor Barger, advocating for the Los Angeles County's Great
  Plates program to continue to serve the City's residents by utilizing
  Pasadena restaurants to provide meals.

  Councilmember McAustin expressed concerns with the costs
  associated with the Great Plates program, however, spoke in favor
  of directing staff to continue the program until February 7, 2021,
  providing time for both the recipients and providers of the program
  to prepare in advance and transition out of the program.

  Councilmember Kennedy spoke in support of Councilmember
  Gordo's suggestion of staff writing an advocacy letter for the Los
  Angeles County's Great Plates program to continue to serve the
  City's residents utilizing Pasadena restaurants to provide meals.

  Council Minutes  4  11/09/2020
   City Clerk Jomsky, read aloud comments from Paul Little,
  representing Pasadena Chamber of Commerce, in favor of the City
  to continue funding the City's Great Plates program.

  Following public comment, it was moved by Councilmember
  McAustin, seconded by CouncilmemberWilson, to approve the staff
  recommendation, with the program to be funded until February 7,
  2021, amended to direct the Mayor to send an advocacy letter to
  the Los Angeles County Supervisor Barger on behalf of the
  residents and businesses in the City, as detailed above:

  AYES: Councilmembers Gordo, Kennedy, Madison, Masuda,
  McAustin, Wilson, Vice Mayor Hampton, Mayor Tornek
  NOES: None
  ABSENT: None
  ABSTAIN: None

  CONSENT ITEMS  AUTHORIZATION TO ENTER INTO CONTRACTS WITH FS
  DISCUSSED SEPARATELY CONTRACTORS, INC., GENTRY GENERAL ENGINEERING,
  INC., AND CEM CONSTRUCTION CORP. FOR AS-NEEDED
  SIDEWALK REPAIR CONSTRUCTION SERVICES IN AN
  AMOUNT NOT-TO-EXCEED $3,000,000 FOR EACH CONTRACT
  Recommendation: It is recommended that the City Council:
  (1) Find the contracts proposed in the agenda report to be
  categorically exempt under the California Environmental Quality Act
  (CEQA) State Guidelines in accordance with Title 14, Chapter 3,
  Article 19, Section 15301, Class 1 - Existing Facilities, which
  exempts minor alteration of existing public facilities where no
  expansion of the use will take place and that there are no features
  that distinguish this project from others in the exempt class and,
  therefore, there are no unusual circumstances;
  (2) Authorize the City Manager to enter into a contract with FS
  Contractors, Inc., for As-Needed Sidewalk Repair Construction
  Services for an amount not-to-exceed $3,000,000 over a five-year
  term, pursuant to Chapter 4.08.135 of the Pasadena Municipal
  Code - Request for Qualifications;
  (3) Authorize the City Manager to enter into a contract with Gentry
  General Engineering, Inc., for As-Needed Sidewalk Repair
  Construction Services for an amount not-to-exceed $3,000,000
  over a five-year term, pursuant to Chapter 4.08.135 of the
  Pasadena Municipal Code - Request for Qualifications; and
  (4) Authorize the City Manager to enter into a contract with CEM
  Construction Corp. for As-Needed Sidewalk Repair Construction
  Services for an amount not-to-exceed $3,000,000 over a five-year
  term, pursuant to Chapter 4.08.135 of the Pasadena Municipal
  Code - Request for Qualifications. (Contract Nos. 31915, 31917,
  and 31920)

  Ara Malayan, Director of Public Works, provided information on the
  City's annual budget related to sidewalk repair, and City Manager
  Mermell provided information on the annual expenditures related to
  the project, with both responding to questions. Kris Markarian, City
  Engineer, provided information on the City's process of prioritizing
  sidewalk repair, and responded to questions.

  Councilmember Gordo expressed concerns with the prioritization of
  sidewalk repair and advocated for work to be prioritized by routes
u  used by the disabled community to access public transportation and
  by the senior community. He requested information on the sidewalk
  repair prioritization list.

  Council Minutes  7  11/09/2020
   Councilmember Kennedy expressed concerns with the prioritization
  of the sidewalk repair in the City and stated his preference that staff,
  with the assistance of Municipal Assistance, Solutions and Hiring
  (MASH) workers, to complete the sidewalk repair throughout the
  City. In addition, he reiterated his request that staff provide an
  updated sidewalk repair program that identifies approximately
  $20,000,000 of repairs of sidewalk replacement that is needed in
  the City. Councilmember Kennedy asked staff to provide
  comprehensive data on mapping out sidewalks using a ranking
  system by greatest need first; and develop options through the
  Finance Committee to pay for such a program. He also requested
  that staff provide information on Economic Development staff's role
  related to business retention in the City, specifically how staff is
  working with local business owners who live in Pasadena, to meet
  the City's qualifications in order to be awarded City contracts.

  Vice Mayor Hampton stated his preference that the City set aside a
  budget for Pasadena-based businesses to provide real
  opportunities to work with the City; and thanked staff for their work
  on sidewalk repair throughout the City.

  City Manager Mermell responded that staff is currently working on
  a report on local procurement that will be presented at a future
  Economic Development and Technology Committee meeting for
  discussion.

  Following discussion, it was moved by Councilmember Masuda,
  seconded by Councilmember Wilson, to approve the staff
